interactions.summary: A student jokes about using DMT as a shortcut, and Jiang dismisses the suggestion as irrelevant to the heavenly-spiritual problem under discussion.
A student proposes repentance and the Lamb of God as the path by which someone could move on from sin.
Jiang answers by making Jesus the hinge of the whole issue: unconditional forgiveness from outside the self is the only solution to the impossible problem of self-redemption.
Students paraphrase Jiang's point as waiting for someone else to save and forgive her, and Jiang guides them to identify that savior as Jesus and then as God.
interactions.speaker_attribution: students paraphrasing with Jiang catechetical prompts

claims.claim: A student proposes repentance and the Lamb of God as the mechanism by which the sinner can be cleansed and move on.
Jiang argues that Jesus matters because he offers a solution to the impossible problem of redeeming a self that believes it deserves its fate.
Jiang says unconditional forgiveness from someone outside the sinner is one viable answer because the sinner cannot forgive herself.
The class distills Jiang's account into a saved-by-another model: the sinner needs someone else to save and forgive her, and that someone is Jesus as God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang names Christianity's center as a rescue from the impossible problem of trying to redeem yourself from inside your own condemned self-understanding.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Jesus is so consequential because he provides a solution. To an impossible problem.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shifts the lecture from moral psychology to grace by making Christ the answer to a problem the self structurally cannot solve.

signature_moments.moment: Unconditional forgiveness becomes, for Jiang, the strongest idea in the universe because it breaks a fate the guilty person already thinks is deserved.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I forgive you unconditionally. I redeem you unconditionally.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's sharpest statement of grace as the only force capable of interrupting self-justifying damnation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The rescue Jesus provides from a spiritual impasse that the sinner cannot resolve alone.
Release from a fate of guilt and passivity through unconditional forgiveness rather than self-repair.
The external absolution the trapped sinner cannot generate for herself and therefore must receive from God.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture's solution phase begins here: after proving that damaged agency cannot restore itself, Jiang shifts to repentance, Jesus, and forgiveness from outside the self.
